data.title: How will parents cope if 5,500+ Nova Scotia school support workers are forced into a provincewide strike?
data.description: In Halifax, Nova Scotia, over 5,500 school support staff members are facing the looming possibility of going on strike within a mere 10 days. Negotiations between eight CUPE (Canadian Union of Public Employees) local branches and the Regional Centres for Education and Conseil Scolaire Acadien Provincial (CSAP) in the province are reaching a critical point. Nelson Scott, the Chair of the Nova Scotia School Board Council of Unions (NSSBCU), expressed concern over the urgency of reaching agreements to safeguard the quality of public education in the region. This unrest follows nearly 10 months of discussions.
